info.title: smista-router HTTP API
info.description: Local-first deterministic model-routing API. See docs/api/http-api.md.

201.description: User created and API key issued

get.description:
The credential-extraction middleware installs the [`RequestCredentials`]
extension only when the caller sent at least one provider key, so the
extractor is optional: its absence simply means no credentials, which still
lists keyless local providers.

Reads the live provider registry off the router and returns one descriptor
per available provider. The order is unspecified, as the registry is keyed
by provider id.

200.description: Turn completed or awaiting input. Buffered as a single `TurnResponse` (`application/json`) or, when the client sends `Accept: text/event-stream`, streamed as Server-Sent Events of `TurnEvent` whose terminal `turn_end` carries the `TurnResponse`.

503.description: Provider credentials missing or fallbacks exhausted

200.description: Turn completed or awaiting input. Buffered as a single `TurnResponse` (`application/json`) or, when the client sends `Accept: text/event-stream`, streamed as Server-Sent Events of `TurnEvent` whose terminal `turn_end` carries the `TurnResponse`.

503.description: Provider credentials missing or fallbacks exhausted
Provider credentials missing or fallbacks exhausted

200.description: Server-Sent Events stream. Each `data:` line is one TurnEvent (internally tagged by `type`, snake_case). Exactly one terminal `turn_end` event carries the TurnResponse payload.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of events to return

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of leading events to skip

ApiError.description: Envelope wrapping the error body under an `error` key.

ApiErrorBody.description:
The structured payload of an [`ApiError`].

`details` carries machine-readable context (such as the offending provider
and model) and is omitted when there is none. It must never contain secrets.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code, for example `missing_provider_credentials`.

message.description: Human-readable, actionable description of what went wrong.

details.description: Optional structured context; never carries secrets.

ApprovalDecision.description:
The decision made on a pending approval.

Each variant serializes to its lowercase name.

ApprovalDecisionEntry.description: A decision for a [`PendingApproval`](super::PendingApproval) with no tool.

approval_id.description: Identifier of the approval the decision applies to.

reason.description: Optional human-readable reason for the decision.

target_type.description: Type of the entity the decision applies to (for example `tool_call`).

target_id.description: Identifier of the entity the decision applies to.

reason.description: Human-readable reason for the decision, if any.

Attachments.description:
Local content the client supplies because the router has no filesystem.

Every file, instruction and skill the task may need from disk travels here.
History, memory and the assembled context are not part of this — the router
owns them.

files.description: Explicit `@path` files included with their content.

instructions.description: Instruction documents the client read from disk.

invoked_skills.description:
Skills the user explicitly invoked, with their full `SKILL.md` body.

Authoritative: routing rules may match on them by name, and their
instructions are added to the model preamble. The router never infers
this set from the prompt.

available_skills.description:
Skills offered for the serving model to activate by reading them.

Same shape as the invoked skills, but distinct by role: they never
influence routing, and the model decides whether to apply one. The full
instructions travel up front, so an activated skill needs no follow-up
fetch.

BootstrapResponse.description:
Response to `POST /auth/bootstrap`, returned once at user creation.

`api_key` is a secret shown only here; the caller must store it securely.
`Debug` is implemented by hand to redact `api_key`, so the credential is
never leaked through `{:?}` formatting, logs, or traces.

user_id.description: Identifier of the created user, for example `user:abc123`.

api_key.description: Long-lived smista API key. Secret; shown only in this response.

Classification.description:
The outcome of intent classification for one request.

Either the user supplied an explicit intent (see [`IntentSource::Explicit`])
or one was inferred deterministically from a matching
[`ClassificationRule`] (see [`IntentSource::Inferred`]). For an inferred
intent, [`matched_rule`](Self::matched_rule) carries the index of the
matching entry in [`ClassificationConfig::rules`] so traces can point back
to the configured rule.

source.description: Whether the intent was given explicitly by the user or inferred.

reason.description: Human-readable explanation of why this intent was chosen.

matched_rule.description:
Index of the matched rule in [`ClassificationConfig::rules`], if any.

Refers to a [`ClassificationRule`].

oneOf.description: Optional deterministic confidence category for an inferred intent.

default_intent.description: Intent used when no rule matches.

intent.description: Intent assigned when the rule matches.

priority.description:
Evaluation priority; rules are evaluated in ascending order (lower
first). Defaults to `1000` when unset.

keywords.description: Keywords; the rule matches when any appears in the prompt.

requires_any_context.description: Required context kinds; the rule matches when any is available.

context.description: What context was included and excluded.

usage.description: Token usage and cost for the turn.

Confidence.description:
Deterministic confidence category for an inferred intent.

This is a coarse signal-strength label, not a probability.

ContextFile.description: A file the client attached, with a content hash and whether it is required.

content_hash.description: Hash of the content, for example `sha256:...`.

required.description:
Whether the file is required (referenced or route-driving) and so cannot
be dropped, as opposed to discardable supplementary context.

ContextInstruction.description: An instruction document the client attached as context.

source.description: Where the instruction came from, for example `SMISTA.md`.

ContextOutcome.description: What context the router included and excluded for a task.

ContextSelectionPayload.description:
Payload of a [`TraceEventType::ContextSelection`] event.

Records a reference to the selected or excluded context — its path and kind —
never the context body itself.

path.description: Path of the referenced context, if it has one.

included.description: Whether the context was included (`true`) or excluded (`false`).

ContinueRequest.description:
Bundle that advances an in-flight run after a continuation.

Every field defaults to empty, so a bare `{}` is a valid no-op and a bare
`{ "interrupt": true }` aborts the in-flight turn with no other input.

tool_results.description: Results of tools the client ran, answering an `awaiting_tool` turn.

approval_decisions.description:
Decisions for approvals with no tool to run, answering an
`awaiting_approval` turn.

decrypted.description: Records the client decrypted, answering an `awaiting_decrypt` turn.

encrypted.description: Records the client encrypted, answering an `awaiting_encrypt` turn.

user_messages.description: User input typed while the run was working, delivered at this boundary.

interrupt.description: Whether to abort the in-flight turn (the Esc path).

cost.description: Estimated cost as a decimal string, if known. Never a float.

CostRange.description:
An estimated cost range in a given currency.

`min` and `max` serialize as decimal strings to preserve monetary precision.

min.description: Lower bound of the estimate, as a decimal string.

max.description: Upper bound of the estimate, as a decimal string.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code for the bounds.

CreateSessionRequest.description:
Body of `POST /sessions`. The title is mandatory.

`encrypted` opts the session into end-to-end encryption and defaults to
`false` when omitted. When it is `true`, `key_id` is required and names the
fingerprint of the per-session key the client holds; when it is `false`,
`key_id` must be absent. The pairing is validated by the router, not by this
type. The choice is fixed for the life of the session.

encrypted.description: Whether the new session is end-to-end encrypted.

key_id.description: Fingerprint of the per-session key, required when `encrypted` is `true`.

CreateSessionResponse.description: Response to `POST /sessions`, wrapping the created session.

model.description: Model used when no rule matches.

fallbacks.description: Models tried, in order, when the default model is unavailable.

Effort.description:
The reasoning effort a model should spend on a routed task.

Declared per routing rule and passed through to the model as its effort
setting. Each variant serializes to its lowercase name. The default is
[`Effort::Medium`].

EncryptedPayload.description:
The sealed wire form of one content payload: an AEAD ciphertext envelope.

Self-describing — it names the algorithm and the key that sealed it, and
carries the one-time nonce and the ciphertext (including its authentication
tag) — and never carries the key itself. It mirrors the envelope storage
persists but is a distinct serialization-first type; the router converts
between the two when it persists or returns content.

version.description: Envelope schema version, so the format can evolve.

key_id.description: Fingerprint of the per-session key that sealed this payload.

nonce.description: Base64-encoded one-time nonce used for this payload.

ciphertext.description: Base64-encoded ciphertext, including the AEAD authentication tag.

ExecutePolicy.description:
The deterministic policy snapshot the client sends with a task.

`version` is the schema version of the snapshot; `source` records how it was
assembled (for example `merged`). The `classification`, `routing`, `tools`
and `privacy` blocks are the canonical [`crate::policy`] types — the same
vocabulary the router evaluates and the CLI loads from `config.toml`.

version.description: Schema version of the policy snapshot.

source.description: How the snapshot was assembled, for example `merged`.

classification.description: Intent-classification rules and the default intent.

tools.description: Tool permission modes, keyed by tool name.

privacy.description: Privacy constraints on the context sent to models.

ExecuteRequest.description: Full input to executing, streaming, or previewing a task.

input.description: What the user is asking for.

workspace.description: Snapshot of the workspace the task runs against.

policy.description: Classification, routing, permission and privacy policy snapshot.

providers.description: Providers available for this request and their credential status.

attachments.description: Local content the router cannot read for itself.

oneOf.description:
For an encrypted session, the sealed form of the user prompt, persisted
as the user message; the plaintext in `input.text` is what calls the
model. Absent for a plaintext session.

GetSessionResponse.description: Response to `GET /sessions/{id}`, wrapping the full session.

IntentSource.description: Origin of the intent attached to a request.

unavailable.description:
Providers omitted from `models` because listing their models failed,
each with the reason it dropped out.

The router queries every configured provider when listing models. A
provider that cannot be listed — most often because its credentials are
missing or were rejected — is left out of `models` and reported here, so
a caller can tell an incomplete result from a genuinely empty one and act
on the cause. Empty when every configured provider was listed.

local_only.description: Restrict routing to local models only.

no_network.description: Forbid any network access for this request.

LocalPrivacy.description:
Privacy constraints for local models.

The effective [`mode`](Self::mode) defaults to [`PermissionMode::Allow`] when
unset: local models may receive context without prompting.

oneOf.description: How sending context to local models is mediated, if set.

MeResponse.description:
Response to `GET /auth/me`, identifying the authenticated user.

Carries only the caller's user ID; it lists no sessions and exposes no
secret values. To enumerate sessions, use `GET /sessions` instead.

Message.description:
A single message in a conversation.

`provider` and `model` identify which model produced an assistant turn; they
are `None` for user, system and tool messages, and may be `None` for an
assistant turn whose origin is unknown.

role.description: The role of the message's author.

content.description: The textual content of the message.

oneOf.description: Provider that produced the message, if applicable.

model.description: Model that produced the message, if applicable.

MessageRole.description:
The role an author plays in a conversation.

Each variant serializes to its lowercase name.

oneOf.description: No authentication is needed, e.g. a local model.
An API key is required.
An API key may be supplied but is not required.
A provider-specific scheme, named by the contained string.

custom.description: A provider-specific scheme, named by the contained string.

ModelAuthRequirement.description:
How a model is authenticated.

Each variant serializes to its snake_case name; [`Self::Custom`] carries the
scheme name as its payload (e.g. `{"custom": "aws-sigv4"}`).

ModelCapabilities.description:
The capabilities a model exposes.

Every flag defaults to `false`, so a [`Default`] value advertises no
capabilities — a conservative starting point a descriptor builds upon.

streaming.description: The model can stream its response incrementally.

json_output.description: The model can be constrained to emit JSON.

system_prompt.description: The model honors a separate system prompt.

memory.description:
The model can drive the memory tool to record and update memory.

Satisfied by tool calling, or — on providers that offer it, such as
OpenAI structured outputs — by a constrained-output equivalent. The
router gates memory orchestration on this flag.

ModelDescriptor.description:
A complete description of a model offered by a provider.

This is also the shape returned for each model by `GET /llm/models`.

model.description: Model name, as defined by the provider.

local.description: Whether the model runs locally (no network call).

max_context_tokens.description: Maximum number of context tokens the model accepts.

max_output_tokens.description: Maximum number of tokens the model emits, if bounded.

input_cost_per_million_tokens.description: Input price per million tokens, serialized as a string for exact precision.

output_cost_per_million_tokens.description: Output price per million tokens, serialized as a string for exact precision.

default_parameters.description: Default generation parameters applied when none are supplied.

max_tokens.description: Maximum number of tokens to generate.

ModelParameters.description:
Sampling and generation parameters for a model invocation.

The typed fields are omitted from serialization when unset. Any keys not
matching a typed field are collected into [`Self::extra`] and re-emitted as
they were, so provider-specific options pass through untouched.

ModelReference.description: A model reference in the form `provider/model`, e.g. `anthropic/claude-sonnet`.

allOf.description: Token and cost totals for the model.

request_count.description: Number of requests served by the model.

ModelUsage.description: Usage attributed to a single model.

oneOf.description: A recorded message.
An intent classification result.
A routing decision.
A context selection or exclusion.
A tool request or execution.
A confirmation decision.
Recorded token usage or cost.

Payload.description:
The decrypted payload of a [`TraceEvent`], tagged by event kind.

Serialized internally tagged under `type` (for example
`{ "type": "message", "role": "user", … }`), so it deserializes on its own
once a sealed payload has been opened. Its variant always matches the
event's [`TraceEventType`].

PendingApproval.description:
A decision the router needs that has no tool to execute.

Raised for disclosures and limits — for example sending context to a remote
model under an `ask` privacy mode, or confirming a cost ceiling. The
`detail` shape depends on `kind`.

approval_id.description: Identifier the approval decision refers to.

kind.description: What kind of decision is being asked for.

detail.description: Machine-readable context for the decision; its shape depends on `kind`.

PermissionMode.description:
How an action is mediated: allowed outright, gated on approval, or blocked.

Used by both tool permissions and privacy (remote/local) policies. Variants
serialize to their lowercase name. The ordering `Allow < Ask < Deny` reflects
increasing strictness, so the stricter of two modes is the greater one — the
layered merge relies on this to ensure a higher layer can only tighten, never
weaken, a mode.

# Examples

```
use smista_core::policy::PermissionMode;

assert!(PermissionMode::Deny > PermissionMode::Ask);
assert_eq!(PermissionMode::Ask.max(PermissionMode::Allow), PermissionMode::Ask);
```

PlainRecord.description:
A storage record paired with its cleartext.

The router sends these in an `awaiting_encrypt` turn (content to seal); the
client returns them in the `/continue` bundle after opening the records of
an `awaiting_decrypt` turn. Correlated by `record_id`.

record_id.description: Identifier of the storage record the cleartext belongs to.

PreviewResponse.description: The predicted routing of a task, without calling the model.

task_type.description: Task type that would be detected.

classification.description: How the task would be classified.

provider.description: Provider that would serve the task.

model.description: Model that would serve the task.

matched_rule.description: Description of the routing rule that would match, if any.

included_context.description: Human-readable descriptions of context that would be included.

excluded_context.description: Human-readable descriptions of context that would be excluded.

estimated_cost.description: Estimated cost range for the task.

restricted_paths.description: Paths treated as sensitive across all model classes.

remote.description: Constraints applied when sending context to remote providers.

local.description: Constraints applied when sending context to local models.

ProviderCredentialInfo.description: A provider available to the request and the credential status of its models.

models.description: Models offered by the provider and their credential status.

ProviderDescriptor.description:
A provider that is available for routing.

This is the shape returned by `GET /llm/providers`, which lists only the
providers that are currently available — those configured with usable
credentials (or a base URL, for local providers). A provider that is not
available is omitted from the listing entirely, so this descriptor carries
no availability flag.

id.description: The provider this descriptor refers to.

local.description:
Whether the provider serves its models locally, with no request leaving
the host or network.

This is the provider-level source of truth for locality: every model the
provider offers inherits it, so a provider can never report itself local
while a model it advertises routes to the cloud. The router uses it as a
routing discriminant to keep sensitive work on local models.

ProviderErrorCategory.description:
Classification of a normalized [`ProviderError`].

Each variant captures a category of failure that the router and API layer
can reason about independently of the provider-specific HTTP status or
SDK error code that produced it. The categories follow the smista.ai
specification (Model interfaces → Error handling).

ProviderModelInfo.description: A model offered by a provider and whether its credential is available.

requires_api_key.description: Whether the model requires an API key.

credential_available.description: Whether a credential for the model is available to the request.

RemotePrivacy.description:
Privacy constraints for remote providers.

The effective [`mode`](Self::mode) defaults to [`PermissionMode::Ask`] when
unset: disclosing context to a remote provider requires approval unless
explicitly allowed.

oneOf.description: How sending context to remote providers is mediated, if set.

blocked_paths.description: Paths that must never be sent to remote providers.

RequiredPermission.description: A permission the task requires and the mode that would apply.

permission.description: Name of the permission, for example `write_files`.

mode.description: Mode that would apply to the permission.

matched_rule.description: Routing rule that matched, if any.

fallback_used.description: Whether a fallback route was used.

override_used.description: Whether a per-request override was used.

RoutingOutcome.description: How a task was routed to a model.

task_type.description: Detected task type that drove routing.

matched_rule.description: Description of the routing rule that matched, if any.

fallback_used.description: Whether a fallback model was used.

override_used.description: Whether an explicit model override was used.

rules.description: Routing rules; evaluated in ascending priority order, first match wins.

oneOf.description: Route used when no rule matches.

RoutingRule.description:
A single deterministic routing rule.

A rule selects [`model`](Self::model) (with optional per-rule
[`fallbacks`](Self::fallbacks)) when all of its present match conditions
hold. Matching is LLM-free. The match conditions are flat and all optional:

- [`intent`](Self::intent): the classified task intent.
- [`paths`](Self::paths): file-path globs; a rule with paths matches when a
  relevant path matches any glob.

A rule with no conditions matches everything (useful as a low-priority
catch-all). Rules are evaluated in ascending [`priority`](Self::priority)
order; the first match wins.

When [`local_only`](Self::local_only) is set, a matched rule must not fall
back to remote models — its fallback chain is restricted to local models.

A matched rule also declares the [`effort`](Self::effort) the model should
spend on the task, defaulting to [`Effort::Medium`].

# Examples

```
use smista_core::effort::Effort;
use smista_core::policy::RoutingRule;

let rule: RoutingRule = serde_json::from_value(serde_json::json!({
    "name": "auth code uses Claude",
    "priority": 30,
    "effort": "high",
    "intent": "edit",
    "paths": ["src/auth/**"],
    "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet",
    "fallbacks": ["openai/gpt-5.5-thinking"],
}))
.unwrap();
assert_eq!(rule.name, "auth code uses Claude");
assert_eq!(rule.priority, 30);
assert_eq!(rule.effort, Effort::High);
assert_eq!(rule.model.model, "claude-sonnet");
assert_eq!(rule.paths, vec!["src/auth/**".to_string()]);
```

priority.description:
Evaluation priority; rules are evaluated in ascending order (lower
first). Defaults to `1000` when unset.

effort.description:
Reasoning effort the model should spend on a matched task. Defaults to
[`Effort::Medium`] when unset.

oneOf.description: Required task intent, if any.

paths.description: File-path globs; when non-empty, a relevant path must match one of them.

local_only.description:
When set, a matched rule must not fall back to remote models; its
fallback chain is restricted to local models.

oneOf.description:
Capability gate: when set, the matched model must satisfy every
capability flagged `true` here.

model.description: Model selected when the rule matches. Using syntax supported by [`ModelReference`] (e.g. `"ollama/llama3"`).

fallbacks.description:
Models tried, in order, when the selected model is unavailable. Subject
to [`local_only`](Self::local_only).

required_permissions.description:
Tool permissions the matched route requires.

Merged over project defaults via [`ToolsConfig::narrow`].

cost_limit.description:
Per-task cost ceiling for the matched route, in account currency.

Serialized as a string for exact precision.

SealedRecord.description:
A storage record paired with its sealed payload.

The router sends these in an `awaiting_decrypt` turn (history to open); the
client returns them in the `/continue` bundle after sealing the content of
an `awaiting_encrypt` turn. Correlated by `record_id`.

record_id.description: Identifier of the storage record the envelope belongs to.

SessionDetail.description:
Full view of a session, returned when it is fetched to be resumed.

Carries the session's `messages` and free-form `metadata`. It omits
`archived`, since archived sessions are not returned on fetch.

encrypted.description: Whether the session's content is end-to-end encrypted.

updated_at.description: When the session was last updated.

SessionSummary.description: Lightweight view of a session, used in listings and on creation.

encrypted.description: Whether the session's content is end-to-end encrypted.

updated_at.description: When the session was last updated.

SignInResponse.description:
Response to `POST /auth/sign-in`, carrying the session token.

`token` is a secret bearer credential; `expires_at` is when it stops being
valid. `Debug` is implemented by hand to redact `token`, so the credential
is never leaked through `{:?}` formatting, logs, or traces.

token.description: Session bearer token. Secret; sent as `Authorization: Bearer`.

expires_at.description: Instant at which the token expires.

revoked.description: Whether the session token was revoked.

Skill.description:
A reusable execution profile defined by a `SKILL.md` file.

[`name`](Self::name) comes from the file's front matter; [`content`](Self::content)
is its Markdown body, which frames the model's behavior for the task. The
same type carries a skill whether it was explicitly invoked or merely offered
for the model to activate; the two cases differ by where the skill travels in
the request, not by shape.

name.description: Machine-readable identifier used to resolve the skill by name.

content.description: The `SKILL.md` body: the behavioral instructions for the model.

status.description: Service liveness indicator; `"ok"` when the server answers.

TaskInput.description: The user's request: prompt text, optional command and explicit model.

oneOf.description: Explicit task command, overriding intent detection when set.
Explicit model to use, bypassing routing when set.

TaskIntent.description:
The kind of work a single step of an AI workflow performs.

Used by smista-router to match a prompt against the user's routing policy.
Each variant serializes to its lowercase name.

allOf.description: Token and cost totals for the task type.

task_type.description: Task type the requests were classified as.

request_count.description: Number of requests of this task type.

TaskTypeUsage.description: Usage attributed to a single task type.

ToolApproval.description:
Whether a client-executed tool needs the user's approval first.

A tool denied by policy never reaches the client, so `deny` is not a value
here.

ToolCallPayload.description:
Payload of a [`TraceEventType::ToolCall`] event.

`arguments`, `result` and `error` are recorded as sanitized references, never
raw tool input or output.

tool_name.description: Name of the tool that was requested or executed.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the tool call.

arguments.description: Reference to the tool arguments, if recorded.

result.description: Reference to the tool result, if recorded.

error.description: Reference to the tool error, if the call failed.

ToolCallStatus.description:
Execution status of a tool call.

**Provisional**: these variants are a placeholder until the private spec
pins the tool-call lifecycle. Serialized as `snake_case`.

ToolRequest.description: A tool the client must execute on the user's machine.

call_id.description: Identifier correlating this call with its later result.

name.description: Name of the tool to invoke.

arguments.description: Arguments for the tool, as a provider-agnostic JSON value.

requires_approval.description: Whether the user must approve the call before it runs.

ToolResult.description:
The result of one client-executed tool, correlated by `call_id`.

For an `ask`-mode tool the user's decision rides [`Self::decision`], so the
approval and the result arrive together.

call_id.description: Identifier matching the originating tool request.

oneOf.description: The user's decision for an `ask`-mode tool, if one was required.

permissions.description: Per-tool permission mode, keyed by tool name.

Trace.description:
The recorded outcome of routing and running a session's tasks.

`events` holds the session's ordered execution events, oldest first. Each
[`TraceEvent`] is self-describing — it carries its own routing context — so
the trace needs no top-level routing fields.

session_id.description: Session the traced tasks belong to.

TraceEvent.description:
A single recorded execution event within a [`Trace`].

Each event carries the routing context of the task that emitted it
(`task_type`, `provider`, `model`, `matched_rule`) and a typed `payload`
whose variant matches `event_type`. For an encrypted session the payload is
sealed, so `event_type` still names the kind without opening it.

task_type.description: Detected intent that drove routing for this event's task.

matched_rule.description: Description of the routing rule that matched, if any.

payload.description: Typed event payload, in clear or sealed.

oneOf.description: The payload in clear, for a non-encrypted session.

plaintext.description: The payload in clear, for a non-encrypted session.

oneOf.description: The payload sealed as an AEAD envelope, for an encrypted session.

encrypted.description: The payload sealed as an AEAD envelope, for an encrypted session.

TraceEventPayload.description:
A [`TraceEvent`]'s payload, in clear or sealed.

A non-encrypted session yields [`Plaintext`](Self::Plaintext) with the typed
[`Payload`]. An end-to-end encrypted session yields
[`Encrypted`](Self::Encrypted) with the sealed [`EncryptedPayload`] envelope;
the router holds no key, so only a client holding the session key can open it
into a [`Payload`].

TraceEventType.description:
The kind of a trace event.

**Provisional**: these variants are a placeholder until the private spec
pins the trace taxonomy. Serialized as `snake_case`.

TraceResponse.description: Envelope wrapping a [`Trace`] under a `trace` key.

oneOf.description: An incremental chunk of generated text.

delta.description: The text appended by this event.

oneOf.description: An incremental chunk of reasoning text, for models that stream it.

delta.description: The reasoning text appended by this event.

oneOf.description: A tool call is forming: its name is known, its arguments still streaming.

call_id.description:
Identifier correlating this event with its later
[`ToolCallRequested`](Self::ToolCallRequested).

name.description: Name of the tool being called.

oneOf.description: The model requested a tool call the client must run.

call_id.description: Identifier correlating this call with its later result.

name.description: Name of the tool to invoke.

arguments.description: Arguments for the tool, as a provider-agnostic JSON value.

requires_approval.description: Whether the user must approve the call before it runs.

allOf.description: Token usage and cost totals for the turn.

oneOf.description: Token usage and cost totals for the turn.

allOf.description:
The terminal event: the turn's outcome, carrying the same
[`TurnResponse`] the buffered call returns (its `status` included).

oneOf.description:
The terminal event: the turn's outcome, carrying the same
[`TurnResponse`] the buffered call returns (its `status` included).

TurnEvent.description:
A single event in a streamed turn.

Serialized with an internally tagged `type` discriminator in snake_case.

allOf.description:
The model finished; an assistant message is included.

Boxed because this is by far the largest variant.

oneOf.description:
The model finished; an assistant message is included.

Boxed because this is by far the largest variant.
The model requested one or more client-executed tools.

tool_requests.description: The tool calls the client must run, correlated by `call_id`.

oneOf.description: The router needs a yes/no decision with no tool to run.

approval.description: The decision the client must obtain.

oneOf.description: The router needs sealed history opened to build the prompt.

records.description: Records the client must decrypt, correlated by `record_id`.

oneOf.description: The router needs its own output sealed before it can be persisted.

records.description: Records the client must encrypt, correlated by `record_id`.

oneOf.description: A terminal error ended the turn.

TurnResponse.description:
The outcome of one turn, returned by `/execute` and `/continue`.

Internally tagged by `status`. A [`Completed`](Self::Completed) turn carries
the assistant message and routing explanation; every other variant is a
continuation the client must act on before resuming the run with
`/continue`, or a terminal [`Error`](Self::Error).

UnavailableProvider.description:
A provider left out of [`ListModelsResponse::models`] because its models
could not be listed.

provider.description: The provider whose models could not be listed.

reason.description: The classification of the failure that left the provider out.

message.description:
Human-readable, redacted detail describing the failure, when the
provider reported one. Never contains credentials.

UpdateSessionRequest.description:
Body of `PUT /sessions/{id}`, updating title and/or archive state.

Each field is optional; omit a field to leave it unchanged.

archived.description: New archive state, if changing it.

Usage.description:
Token usage and cost metadata for a single model invocation.

All fields are optional and omitted from serialization when unset.

cached_tokens.description: Input tokens served from a provider cache.

reasoning_tokens.description: Tokens spent on reasoning, when reported separately.

total_tokens.description: Total tokens, when the provider reports a combined count.

estimated_cost.description: Cost estimated before the invocation, serialized as a decimal string.

actual_cost.description: Cost reconciled after the invocation, serialized as a decimal string.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code for the costs; defaults to `USD` when absent.

UsageBreakdown.description: A session's usage total and its per-model and per-task-type breakdowns.

total.description: Combined usage across the whole session.

by_task_type.description: Usage attributed to each task type.

UserMessage.description: A message the user typed while the run was working.

Workspace.description: Snapshot of the workspace a task runs against.

root.description: Absolute path to the workspace root.

git_branch.description: Current git branch, if the workspace is a git repository.

active_file.description: The file the user is actively editing, if any.

apiKey.name: X-Smista-Api-Key
apiKey.description: User API key, presented only at sign-in
